newsitem.title: USA: IMF makes progress on selected SDR allocation.
newsitem.headline: IMF makes progress on selected SDR allocation.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund is making progress toward an agreement on a limited issue of Special Drawing Rights (SDRs), its artificial currency, a senior IMF official said on Thursday.
First Deputy Managing Director Stanley Fischer said IMF management was seeking an allocation of up to 26 billion SDRs, worth about $37-1/2 billion at current exchange rates.
The money would be issued to new IMF members such as Russia and other countries that have not fully participated in past SDR allocations.
"We are working toward an agreement on an SDR allocation on equity grounds," Fischer told a news conference.
He also expects agreement soon on a plan to double the amount of resources the IMF can draw on in financial emergencies such as the one that afflicted Mexico last year.
The agreement could come in a few weeks time and would involve the creation of a "New Arrangements to Borrow" for the IMF that likely would be financed by more than 20 of its member nations, he said.
